title: The next and brief skills ask through the host's named question tool, not "this host's own question tool"
name: next-brief-ask-slot
description: `plugins/skills/next/SKILL.md` and `plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md` say "ask a yes or a no with this host's own question tool" in their own words and never render the `{{ask}}` slot, so on Codex the approval and merge questions — the two the original report (node codex-asks-with-request-user-input-by-na-zfq5) was about — still name no tool, while `decide` and `loop` now do. Put the `{{ask}}` slot into both skills where the yes/no is asked (step 2 and step 5 of next, the approval step of brief), and cut the sentence it replaces so the rule is not stated twice. The slot text is already per host in `plugins/hosts/*.json`; nothing there changes. `pnpm plugins` regenerates all four hosts' skills — commit them with the source. Extend `test/integration/plugin.test.ts`: the existing "codex names its own question tool" test loops over `decide`, `loop`, `next`, `brief`; add the mirror for `claude` (`AskUserQuestion` in next and brief) and the paste-rule test stays green. Check `packages/claude-code-plugin/skills/next/SKILL.md` and `.../brief/SKILL.md` by eye once: the slot must land in the sentence that asks, not beside it.

brief.approach:
The first run put the existing `{{ask}}` slot into next and brief. That slot is written for `decide`: it says "pass `decide` exactly the option they picked" and repeats the explicit-yes and on-their-behalf rules, so next step 2, next step 5 and brief step 3 now state those rules twice and carry a `decide` instruction where no `decide` is called. The work on the branch is kept and corrected.

1. Add a second slot, `askYes`, to each of plugins/hosts/claude.json, codex.json, cursor.json and opencode.json. It is the yes/no form of that host's `ask` text and never mentions `decide`:
   - claude: ask with AskUserQuestion, this host's own question tool — one question, a yes and a no.
   - codex: ask with `request_user_input`; keep the existing fallback wording ("When it is not listed", ask in the conversation) and the note that Codex's own prompt keeps `request_user_input` away from permission requests, so the yes may come in the chat.
   - cursor: this host's own question tool, a yes and a no.
   - opencode: no question tool — ask in the conversation and wait for a reply.
   Each ends with the rule once: a yes in the chat is a yes, silence is not, never answer on their behalf.
2. In plugins/skills/next/SKILL.md (steps 2 and 5) and plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md (step 3), replace the `{{ask}}` slot the first run added with `{{askYes}}`, and cut the sentences it duplicates, so each step says once: ask the yes/no (the slot), call `approve` / `accept` with `confirmed: true` only on an explicit yes, and what happens on a no. Keep the paste-before-ask sentence in step 5 of next exactly as it is, and keep the plain-language explanation wording of step 2 and brief step 3 as development has it now.
3. `{{ask}}` in decide and loop is unchanged.
4. Run `pnpm plugins` and commit the four hosts' generated copies with the source.
5. Extend test/integration/plugin.test.ts:
   - the codex test covers next and brief too: both contain `request_user_input` and `When it is not listed`;
   - claude next and brief contain `AskUserQuestion`; opencode next and brief contain neither tool name;
   - for every host, the generated next and brief contain no "exactly the option" (no `decide` instruction), and "only on an explicit yes" appears once in brief and twice in next (step 2 and step 5);
   - update the comment that says next and brief do not name the tool.
6. Check packages/claude-code-plugin/skills/next/SKILL.md and .../brief/SKILL.md by eye once: each step reads as one ask, one rule.

acceptance.run: pnpm plugins && git diff --exit-code -- packages plugins
acceptance.proves: The generated skills for all four hosts are regenerated from the source and committed; nothing is left out of date.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run --project integration test/integration/plugin.test.ts
acceptance.proves: next and brief name each host's question tool, carry no `decide` instruction, state the explicit-yes rule once per step, and decide/loop plus the paste rule are unchanged.
The test and the host files pass lint and format.
